prompt: A runner has covered $100$ m at $15$ seconds and $400$ m at $75$ seconds. What is her average speed between those two split times, in meters per second?
hint: Average speed is the slope between the two split points: change in distance over change in time.

hints.text: Average speed is the slope between the two split points: change in distance over change in time.
Distance change: $400 - 100 = 300$ m. Time change: $75 - 15 = 60$ s.

explanation: Use average rate of change = change in distance ÷ change in time.

alternativeExplanations.title: Rise over run on a graph
steps: Plot (15, 100) and (75, 400) with time across and distance up.
Draw the straight line joining them: the rise is 300 and the run is 60.
Slope = 300 ÷ 60 = 5. Average speed IS the slope of that connecting line.

alternativeExplanations.title: Only the gap matters
steps: Do not divide 400 by 75 — that averages her whole race, starting gun included.
The question asks only about the stretch BETWEEN the two splits, so subtract both times and both distances first.
300 m in 60 s is 5 m/s. The whole-race average is about 5.3 m/s, so subtracting first really does change the answer.
